item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very late here, but:

The Foundation would love to hear your theories, if you have any. They don't seem to have a clue. It seems to work, so it keeps people alive, and it's a lot easier to clean up than what SCP-939 do. So, they huff, and they puff, and they magic white smoke the bad things away. That's what matters in matters of immediacy; that it works.

That's as much of the matter as is understood by the Foundation, presently. It warrants consideration, from in- and out-of-universe perspectives, but currently, strictly a niggling unknown; something to think about.

That's what we thought about when we decided to put that detail there, and there is a reason. Just, the Foundation doesn't quite know it, so it isn't presented as being understood by them.

In short, good question. I don't remember for sure if the reason was hinted at elsewhere, but you might enjoy looking in any case. That's why we're here, isn't it? To be confused, and hope it passes. I think the answer was hinted at, but I can't remember; this was written years ago, and I'm sure it was only hints given, never conclusions. If it was just gonna be told, what would the point be?

If you think you figure it out, let me know what you think. I might remember.

Water charges are used in breaching structures. Consists of an explosive backed with water - serves to focus the blast toward the door to be opened and minimizes blast effects and shrapnel the breaching team has to deal with.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is solid, upvoted.

Two things I can think of that might improve it a bit. One, what's a water charge, and why was it used? Two, it gets a bit confusing that the agents refer to one another by designation but are referenced by name. I suggest making sure it's clear in the initial documentation who's who, and the logs are formatted to show their designations rather than names so it's easier to keep straight.
